_readme: Strings that must never reach a public page, checked by scripts/lint-content.ts.
Each rule has a `pattern` (case-insensitive regex), a `why`, and optional `files`
limiting it to matching paths. Global rules apply to every file under content/.
corpus/profile.md, and the per-project claim constraints in each dossier.

rules.why: CodebaseQA's retired line count. The corpus measured ~24,400 and retired this figure as roughly 40% high.
Retired Pond figures; the corpus marks them disputed and unverified.
Unsupported superlative: zero corpus hits, never claimed on a resume.
No corpus record of a 23-question flow. The defensible fact is the share of accounts created through it.
The experiment had four variants (facts.md, measured).
A comparative claim about an employer's internal product.
Stale status. Full-time Software Engineer at QuinStreet since June 2026.
Retired address; a school account after graduation is a silent failure mode.
The resume says San Francisco, and the site must match the document a recruiter reads next to it.
The QuinStreet internship was full-time for twelve months.
Same title both phases: the corpus wording is 'converted to full-time'.
The trading system is a project, never an employer, and the repo name carries a person's name.
The trading system has never placed an order; no P&L claim exists.
Relevant Priors must not carry the company's name until the repo is renamed.
No revenue figure about a public company goes on a personal site.
Incident exposure detail is the employer's to disclose, not his.
Year One executive-brief metrics; magnitudes only until Shree clears them.
Internal product KPIs from the same brief.
Employer defect-rate absolutes; the ratio is the publishable form.
Withheld in corpus/skills.md: no dossier evidences them, so they are traps in a screen.
Placeholder left in copy.
The DuckDB write-up is a six-page paper in ACM format with no venue.
'Led' was retired for the DeepTek internship as an overclaim.
DeepTek used Node.js with OAuth 2.0 and RBAC.
EchoLens's award is unresolved: the corpus says LA Hacks, the only public record is a different event with no winner ribbon.
Most of these projects were agent-built; the disclosure is the point.
